ambiguities.text: The specification does not detail the exact criteria for is_reusable_validator() — only that the validator must be inactive.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume is_reusable_validator() requires the validator to have exited and been fully withdrawn, with a sufficient cooldown period to prevent timing attacks.

ambiguities.text: The timing relationship between index allocation and on_reused_index() is not explicitly specified — whether they must be atomic.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume on_reused_index() is called immediately after index allocation in the same state transition, ensuring no window where the new validator inherits equivocation status.

implicit_assumptions.description: The system assumes that a new validator assigned a reused index is a distinct entity with no relationship to the previous validator that held that index.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A slashed validator could re-enter the system with a clean equivocation record by re-depositing and receiving their old index, evading fork choice penalties.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot time deposits to deliberately receive a specific reused index for strategic advantage.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: An attacker could target specific indices to clear equivocation records or manipulate fork choice weights by controlling which indices are reused.
